answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may submit jobs or earn fees. Repeatedly creating identities then does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must tie up more capital per identity, and provable misconduct—such as double-spending a task claim—destroys the deposit. A crystal-clear atlas of public stakes lets others verify the cost, while pigment in a profile is merely cosmetic and grants no extra weight.
